title: King David Hotel Jerusalem: Exodus Hotel Guide
description: Stay at the King David Hotel in Jerusalem, where scenes of the 1960 film Exodus were shot. Film facts, history and tips for visiting.
h1: King David Hotel Jerusalem: the real hotel from Exodus
intro: Built from pink Jerusalem limestone, the King David Hotel has watched over the Old City since 1931. It also has a small part in film history: Otto Preminger's Exodus shot scenes here.
filming: Several scenes of the 1960 film Exodus were shot at the hotel, outside as well as inside, including in the main lobby and on the terrace. A scene starring Paul Newman was filmed on that terrace. The film as a whole was shot on location around Israel, including Jerusalem.
facts: The hotel opened in 1931 and was founded by the Egyptian Jewish banker Ezra Mosseri.
It is built of locally quarried pink limestone and looks out over the Old City and Mount Zion.
Its guest list has included kings, presidents and film stars, among them Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton.
In July 1946 an attack on the hotel's southern wing, which housed British administration offices, became one of the best-known events of the Mandate period.
visit: The hotel sits on King David Street in the centre of Jerusalem, within reach of the Old City. Ask for a room facing the walls if the view matters to you, and have a coffee on the terrace even if you stay elsewhere.
